references.text: Describes Ishmael's nature as a 'wild donkey of a man' and his future, which is fulfilled in his life as an archer in the wilderness.
God's promise to bless Ishmael and make him into a great nation, reflected in that God was with the boy.
God hears the boy's cry and intervenes – the immediate context for why God was with Ishmael.
Ishmael's twelve sons and their settlements in the wilderness, showing the fulfillment of God being with him and his growing up in the desert.
A typological parallel between Isaac's and John the Baptist's upbringing in the wilderness under God's protection before their public ministry.
